title: Platform systems & services - Team wiki, runbooks, dashboards, alerts, and roadmap (Q4 2026)
author: Alex Kim
body:
Summary:
This page is the canonical team wiki entry for Platform systems & services - Team wiki, runbooks, dashboards, alerts, and roadmap (Q4 2026).

1) Intro & scope
This document covers the production platform services owned by the Platform team: platform-api, control-plane, autoscaler, metrics-ingest, kv-cache, batch-workers, and observability (Grafana/Prometheus/Tempo). It describes service owners, SLOs, alert thresholds, escalation paths, runbook steps for common incidents, and the high-level roadmap for Q4 2026.

2) Systems & Services inventory (short)
- platform-api - REST/gRPC API layer for internal control plane (owner: Platform API squad).
- control-plane - orchestration, deployment control, rollout policies (owner: Orchestration squad).
- autoscaler - workload-aware GPU scaling and burst policies (owner: Autoscale squad).
- metrics-ingest - timeseries ingestion, rollups, and retention (owner: Observability squad).
- kv-cache - prefix/KV caching service used by serving runtime (owner: Serving Runtime).
- batch-workers - batch job processing (owner: Batch squad).
- observability - Grafana, Prometheus, Tempo, central alert manager (owner: Observability squad).

3) SLOs & service-level indicators (must be referenced in alerts and runbooks)
- platform-api: Availability 99.95% monthly, p95 request latency < 120ms (steady-state).
- control-plane: Successful deploys 99.9%, median rollouts < 60s per shard.
- autoscaler: Scale decisions applied within 30s 95% of the time.
- metrics-ingest: Ingestion success > 99.5% with 7-day delayed repair window.
- kv-cache: Cache hit rate > 70% for customer-prefix workloads.

4) Dashboards (Grafana) - canonical panels and ownership
- Cluster Overview dashboard (grafana/dashboard/cluster-overview) - owner: eng-platform-observability. Key panels: node healthy count, cluster CPU/GPU utilization (per-region), pod restarts, pending pods.
- Service Health dashboard (grafana/dashboard/service-health) - owner: each service squad. Panels: error rate, p50/p95 latencies, request rate, backlog/queue depth.
- Autoscaler Insights (grafana/dashboard/autoscaler-insights) - owner: Autoscale squad. Panels: scaling events, decision latency, cold-starts, rejected requests due to capacity.
- Cost & efficiency dashboard - owner: FinOps / Platform. Panels: GPU utilization vs reserved capacity, prefix cache effectiveness, per-route token-cost breakdown.

Dashboard tips:
- Use the time-range quick selector: 5m/1h/24h. For incidents, start with 15m and step back to 6h.
- Annotate incidents directly on Grafana (team lead or incident commander).

5) Alerting defaults (Alertmanager)
Alert naming convention: PLAT.<SERVICE>.<SEVERITY>.<METRIC> e.g., PLAT.AUTOSCALER.P1.SCALE_FAILED
Default severities: P1 (site impacting), P2 (user-impacting), P3 (degradation/ops exposure).
Key alert thresholds (examples):
- PLAT.PLATFORM-API.P1.ERR_RATE: error_rate > 1% sustained for 5m AND request_rate > 10rps.
- PLAT.CONTROL-PLANE.P1.DEPLOY_FAIL_RATE: failing_deploys > 2 in 30m.
- PLAT.AUTOSCALER.P1.SCALE_DELAY: average_scale_decision_latency > 30s for 5m.
- PLAT.METRICS-INGEST.P2.INGEST_LAG: ingestion_lag > 5m for 10m.
- PLAT.KV-CACHE.P2.HITRATE_DROP: hit_rate drops > 20% from baseline for 10m.
- Infra P1: node_gpu_utilization > 95% for 10m AND pending_pods > 20.

Escalation routing:
- P1 alerts page to on-call primary (SMS + Slack @channel), then to team lead after 5m, Eng Director after 15m if unresolved.
- P2 alerts page to on-call primary (Slack DM), auto-create Jira ops ticket with prefix "ops/".

6) Runbooks - common incident playbooks (step-by-step)
A) High error rate on platform-api (PLAT.PLATFORM-API.P1.ERR_RATE)
1. Acknowledge alert in PagerDuty/Alertmanager.
2. Open the Service Health dashboard -> platform-api. Check error breakdown by endpoint and by region.
3. Run: kubectl get pods -n platform | grep platform-api to check pod restarts and recent events.
4. Check frontend logs (Stackdriver/Elasticsearch): query by trace id sample and correlation ID.
5. If recent deploy observed in last 15m: rollback to previous revision: kubectl rollout undo deployment/platform-api -n platform --to-revision=<previous_rev>.
6. If CPU/memory saturation found: scale replicas: kubectl scale deployment/platform-api --replicas=<n>.
7. If DB or upstream issue suspected: check control-plane and metrics-ingest; escalate to respective owners.
8. Post-incident: join retrospective, annotate Grafana and create action items.

B) Autoscaler failing to add capacity (PLAT.AUTOSCALER.P1.SCALE_FAILED)
1. Confirm alert details in Autoscaler Insights.
2. Check controller logs: kubectl logs deployment/autoscaler -n platform --tail=200.
3. Verify cloud provider quotas and recent failures: aws ec2 describe-spot-instance-requests / GCP equivalent.
4. If quota issue: submit immediate quota increase using cloud console and escalate to infra pager.
5. Temporarily increase burst capacity policy: update configmap platform/autoscaler-config -> field burst_pool_size and restart deploy.
6. If root cause is scheduling constraints, check taints/tolerations and node selectors.

7) Incident retrospective template (use for P1/P2)
- Incident summary (short).
- Timeline (first alert -> mitigation -> resolution).
- Root cause analysis.
- Actions (owners + due dates).
- Severity and SLO impact.
- Postmortem reviewer list and distribution.

8) Onboarding / How-tos (quick tasks)
- Add a new dashboard: copy dashboard template (grafana/template/platform-service.json), update variables and panels, save with folder "Platform / Service Health", add owner in dashboard metadata.
- Create alert rule: start from alert-template.yaml, update prometheus expr, labels (team, severity), and add to gitops repo: infra/monitoring/rules/<service>-alerts.yaml.
- Deploy a canary: update rollout strategy in k8s manifest: add canary weight and use control-plane canary API: curl -X POST $CONTROL_PLANE/canary -d '{"service":"<svc>","weight":10}'.

9) Roadmap highlights - Q4 2026 (high-level milestones)
- M1 (Oct): Autoscaler v2 alpha - support workload-aware burst and region-aware routing. Owner: Autoscale squad.
- M2 (Nov): Unified cost dashboard + per-customer cost attribution (FinOps + Platform).
- M3 (Nov): Standardized runbook templates and editorial pass across all services.
- M4 (Dec): Private deployment observability package: deployable Grafana+Prometheus helm chart and hardened alerting defaults.
- Ongoing: Improve KV cache hit rate via adaptive prefetch (target +10% hit rate by EOY).

10) Ownership & contacts
- Primary on-call: refer to rota: /confluence/eng-platform/oncall-rotations (on-call pager covered by Platform team).
- Service owners: listed in section 2. For urgent escalation use Slack channel #plat-ops and page the on-call.

11) Documentation hygiene & contribution process
- All dashboard changes must be made via PR to infra/monitoring and linked to a Jira.
- Runbooks updated? Update this page and add entry to related_pages with PR link.
- Quarterly review: every quarter the Platform docs owner runs a doc-health audit and assigns owners for stale pages.

Appendix A - Example alert rule (Prometheus YAML snippet)
apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
kind: PrometheusRule
metadata:
  name: platform-api-alerts
  namespace: monitoring
spec:
  groups:
  - name: platform-api.rules
    rules:
    - alert: PLAT_PLATFORM_API_ERR_RATE
      expr: sum(rate(http_server_errors_total{service="platform-api"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{service="platform-api"}[5m])) * 100 > 1
      for: 5m
      labels:
        severity: page
        team: platform-api
      annotations:
        summary: "platform-api error rate > 1% (5m)"

Appendix B - Useful commands
- kubectl get pods -n platform
- kubectl describe pod <pod> -n platform
- kubectl rollout status deployment/<svc> -n platform
- terraform plan -target=module.monitoring

If anything in this page conflicts with team-specific runbooks, follow the service-specific runbook and notify docs owner for reconciliation. This page is maintained by the Platform docs owner (contact: alex.kim@redwood-inference.com).
